title: Checking the summary against the code
intro: I kept layers and worked through one task in Formbricks #8650: check a summary, follow the access guard, then get back to the call. I explored behavior, counterexamples, impact and author handoff first. I chose M because I could work with this PR’s content and keep the existing review model.
rows: Six summary points share L49–130. I still have to find the lines behind each point.
I gave each point a smaller target. The full wording and surrounding code stay available so I can check beyond the highlight.
The access check continues in another file.
Inspect guard opens both checks. Return brings me back to the caller’s selection and reading position. I mapped this route manually.
File and display actions sit across several controls.
I put file actions beside the filename and display settings above the code. Less-used tools sit in named menus, which adds a click.
tradeoff_title: Why I kept one code pane
tradeoff: Showing the caller and guard together squeezed both at laptop width, so I chose Return. Both comparison screens use Unified. The original fits more code; M gives files and summary links more room. Focus gives that space back.
validation: I kept the PR details, icons, layer numbers and file positions visible. The 0/7 count is for this sample; the PR has 52 files. Visiting a file leaves progress alone. Mark viewed changes it; Undo reverses it.
next: I’d ask developers to explain the access check on both screens, then find something the summary might miss. I’d watch for wrong turns and missed branches. If smaller highlights lead people to overlook code, I’d change them.
scope: This prototype covers seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2. Links are manually mapped. The PR is merged; Submit is disabled. Semantic diffs and modified-file review are outside this sample. I have not tested it with developers.
